_meta.title: Varṇa word-formation lexicon — worldly (bīja) reading, consonants only
_meta.purpose: The reading USED IN WORD FORMATION is the worldly/bīja propensity of each varṇa. For most consonants this is a binding/negative propensity (an affliction); for a few (ca, ra, va, sa, ha, kṣa) the worldly root Sarkar assigns is itself sustaining/positive, so it is NOT forced negative here.
_meta.source: P.R. Sarkar (Shrii Shrii Anandamurti), 'Acoustic Roots of the Indo-Aryan Alphabet' (1984-85, Calcutta; pub. Ananda Marga Philosophy in a Nutshell Pt 8 / Discourses on Tantra Vol 1).
_meta.derivation: primary field `worldly_vritti` = the propensity Sarkar assigns to the varṇa, verified line-by-line against the source PDF. `counter_pole` = a DERIVED antithesis (NOT in the source, which gives only the one worldly root per consonant).
cleanup_vs_authoritative: Corrected the 5 inverted entries where the authoritative file put an INVENTED negative on the worldly slot but Sarkar's actual root is positive: ca (viveka, not aviveka), va (dharma, not adharma), sa (mokṣa, not escapism), ha (parā-vidyā, not avidyā), kṣa (aparā-vidyā, not mithyā-jñāna). Here the worldly_vritti holds Sarkar's actual root and the invented negative is demoted to counter_pole (type=worldly_distortion).
ra: worldly_vritti = vitality/fire (Sarkar's primary emphasis); sarvanāśa kept as its binding counter.
All counter-poles relabeled as DERIVED. Shared remedies kept, not fabricated apart (see _counter_pole_note).
_meta._counter_pole_note: Counter-poles are derived, not from Sarkar. Several legitimately COINCIDE — one virtue counters several afflictions (Vinaya/humility counters both ahaṁkāra and dambha; Jāgaraṇa/awakening counters both jāḍya and mūrcchā; Kṣamā/forgiveness both anutāpa and krodha; Viveka both as ca's root and na's remedy). These coincidences are retained deliberately; inventing distinct antonyms to remove them would be post-hoc fabrication.
_meta._status: FAITHFUL DOCTRINAL TRANSCRIPTION — verified against the source. NOT empirically validated: the pre-registered blind signal tests on this lexicon returned NO_SIGNAL (real ≈ scrambled). This file is for word-formation reading / contemplative authoring, not a validated sound→meaning decoder.
_meta.scope: consonants (33 + kṣa); vowels intentionally omitted per request.
_meta.polarity_values: binding = worldly affliction | sustaining = liberative root | mundane = neutral knowledge
_meta.fields: worldly_vritti, polarity, element (where Sarkar states a tattva), counter_pole{sanskrit,english,type,derived}, source_quote

ka.element: flowing water (ka = water; 'that which produces sound')
ka.source_quote: Ka is the acoustic root of the abhīpsātmaka āśā vṛtti. It is also the acoustic root of Kārya Brahma.

kha.source_quote: The acoustic root of cintā vṛtti [worry] is kha. Impersonal thoughts are symbolized by kha.

worldly_vritti.english: effort / striving to arouse dormant potential

ga.source_quote: The effort made to arouse one's dormant potentiality is called ceṣṭā. Ga is the acoustic root of ceṣṭā vṛtti.

worldly_vritti.english: attachment / love bound by time, space, individuality

gha.source_quote: Mamatā, the vṛtti of love and attachment, is related to time, space and individuality. Gha is the acoustic root of mamatā vṛtti.

nga.source_quote: Uṋa is the acoustic root of dambha vṛtti [the propensity of vanity].

ca.source_quote: Ca is the acoustic root of viveka [conscience].

worldly_vritti.english: nervous breakdown / collapse of a functioning mind

cha.source_quote: Cha is the acoustic root of vikalatā vṛtti [nervous breakdown].

ja.source_quote: Ja is the acoustic root of ahaṁkāra vṛtti (ego). The ego becomes inflated when one allows one's 'I' feeling to take a predominant role.

jha.source_quote: Jha is the acoustic root of lolupatā, lobha [greed] and lolatā [avarice] vṛttis.

nya.source_quote: Iṋa is the acoustic root of kapaṭatā vṛtti [hypocrisy].

tta.source_quote: Ṭa is the acoustic root of vitarka vṛtti [overstating one's case]. Vitarka is a combination of a bad temper and garrulousness.

ttha.source_quote: Ṭha is the acoustic root of anutāpa vṛtti [repentance].

dda.source_quote: Ḍa is the acoustic root of lajjā vṛtti [the propensity of shyness].

ddha.source_quote: Senseless, sadistic killing is called piśunatā vṛtti. [Ḍha is its acoustic root.]

nna.source_quote: Ṇa is the acoustic root of īrṣā vṛtti [the propensity of envy].

worldly_vritti.english: staticity, deep sleep, intellectual dullness, spiritual inertia

ta.source_quote: Ta is the acoustic root of staticity, long sleep and deep sleep, and of intellectual dullness and spiritual inertness.

tha.source_quote: Tha is the acoustic root of viṣāda vṛtti, of melancholy.

da.source_quote: Da is the acoustic root of peevishness.

worldly_vritti.english: thirst for acquisition (wealth, name, fame, power, prestige)

dha.source_quote: Dha is the acoustic root of thirst for acquisition. This limitless craving is called tṛṣṇā in Sanskrit.

worldly_vritti.english: blind attachment / infatuation (deśa, kāla, idea, ādhāra)

na.source_quote: Na is the acoustic root of moha vṛtti [blind attachment or infatuation].

pa.source_quote: Pa is the acoustic root of ghṛṇā vṛtti [hatred or revulsion]. Pa is the acoustic root of the fetter of hatred.

pha.source_quote: Pha is the acoustic root of bhaya vṛtti [the propensity of fear].

ba.source_quote: Ba is the acoustic root of avajñā vṛtti [indifference].

worldly_vritti.english: deluded obsession (loss of common sense under a ripu's spell)

bha.source_quote: Bha is the acoustic root of the mūrcchā vṛtti. It means to lose one's common sense under the hypnotic spell of a particular ripu.

worldly_vritti.english: annihilation; and giving latitude / indulgence (Hindi baṛhvā denā)

ma.source_quote: Ma is the acoustic root of praṇāśa [annihilation]. It is also the acoustic root of praśraya vṛtti – giving latitude [indulgence].

worldly_vritti.english: lack of confidence (in self and others); also constant movement

ya.element: constant movement (like the movement of air)
ya.source_quote: Ya is the acoustic root of aviśvāsa vṛtti [lack of confidence], and is also the acoustic root of constant movement (like the movement of air).

counter_pole.english: defeatist annihilation-thought ('everything is gone, I am undone')

ra.source_quote: Ra is the acoustic root of agnitattva or prāṇaśakti – vitality. It is also the acoustic root of sarvanāśa [the thought of annihilation]. The monosyllabic word ra means 'fire'.

la.source_quote: La is the acoustic root of krūratā vṛtti [cruelty]. La is also the acoustic root of kṣititattva, the solid factor.

worldly_vritti.english: ensconcement in one's original stance; the sustaining principle

counter_pole.english: deviation from original stance / loss of sustaining order

va.source_quote: Va is the acoustic root of dharma. Va is also the acoustic root of jalatattva [the liquid factor], and of the rain-god Varuṇa Deva.

worldly_vritti.english: the mutative principle; psychic longing / material pursuit (artha)

counter_pole.english: transmutation of dynamism into purposeful accomplishment

sha.source_quote: Śa is the acoustic root of rajoguṇa [the mutative principle]. It is also the acoustic root of artha [psychic longing].

worldly_vritti.english: the static principle; all physical / worldly desires (kāma)

ssa.source_quote: Ṣa is the acoustic root of tamoguṇa [the static principle], and of all kinds of worldly desires … kāma.

sa.source_quote: Sa is the acoustic root of mokṣa [unqualified liberation]. Sa is the acoustic root of sattvaguṇa [the sentient principle].

worldly_vritti.english: intuitional science; ethereal factor, daytime, the sun, svarloka

ha.source_quote: Ha is the acoustic root of the ethereal factor, of daytime, of the sun, of svarloka, and of parā-vidyā [intuitional science].

ksha.source_quote: Kṣa is the acoustic root of mundane knowledge, and is also the acoustic root of material science.
